title: Chapter 6 – Cost Behavior & Cost Estimation (Objectives)
notes: Describe key characteristics and graphs of various cost behaviors
Use cost equations to express and predict costs
Use account analysis and scatterplots to analyze cost behavior
Use the high-low method to analyze cost behavior
Use regression analysis to analyze cost behavior
Describe variable costing and prepare a contribution margin income statement

flashcards.front: Cost behaviors: variable vs fixed vs mixed vs step.
flashcards.back: Variable: total ↑ with volume; Fixed: total constant in relevant range; Mixed: fixed + variable; Step: jumps at thresholds.
Cost behavior assumptions hold only within the normal capacity/activity band.
y = f + vx, where f=fixed, v=variable rate, x=activity; predict cost at a given x.

flashcards.front: Total vs Average cost with volume change.
flashcards.back: Total fixed unchanged; average fixed ↓ as volume ↑; variable total changes with x.
Classify accounts as fixed/variable/mixed; visualize cost-volume relationship and detect outliers.
Pick highest and lowest activity points → v = Δcost/Δactivity → f = total − v×x → cost equation.
Simple, quick; uses only two points, sensitive to outliers.
Uses all data points to fit best line; provides R², intercept (f), slope (v); tests significance.
Proportion of variance in cost explained by activity; higher is generally better (context matters).

flashcards.front: Variable vs Absorption costing: key difference.
flashcards.back: Absorption inventories fixed MOH in product cost (required for GAAP); Variable treats fixed MOH as period cost (internal).
Sales − Variable costs = CM; CM − Fixed costs = Operating income.
